summary: A reply from Rand to RFC 111, which asked sites for implementation schedules. It restates the memo's two goals: realistic schedules, and sharing of techniques that worked. The author had not yet prodded sites because the schedules depend on Telnet, and no Telnet specification was available to everyone.

eli5.summary: A helper answers the teacher: I understand the due-date plan, but we cannot say when we will finish because we still do not have the instructions for one part.

subtitle: Rand answers a 1971 request for implementation schedules and explains why it is waiting for a TELNET specification.

tldr.problem: RFC 111 asked sites for implementation schedules, but the schedules depend on TELNET, which had no specification known to everyone.
tldr.mechanism: J. Heafner of Rand restates the goals of RFC 111, says he will contact site liaisons once a TELNET RFC appears, and plans to publish the schedules as an update to NIC Memo 5767.
tldr.outcome: Schedules would be collected by phone, mail or NIC and edited by Alex McKenzie of BBN before publication as an RFC.

today: RFC 130 updates RFC 111, and its own status is listed as Unknown. It is a historical status note and has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Two Goals of RFC 111
sections.content: J. Heafner of Rand reads RFC 111 ("Pressure from the chairman") as having two aims. The first is to set realistic implementation schedules and publish them so everyone can plan productive use of Network services. The second is to uncover implementation techniques and strategies that worked best and could help future implementations.
sections.eli5: The teacher wants everyone to say when they will finish, and also to share tricks that helped.

sections.title: Waiting for TELNET
sections.content: Heafner has not yet asked host teams for schedules, because they include TELNET and no specification is known to everyone. Tom O'Sullivan of Raytheon (TELNET Chairman) and John Melvin of SRI advise that a TELNET RFC will be generated soon. Heafner will then contact the site liaisons.
sections.eli5: You cannot say when a puzzle will be done if one piece of the instructions is still missing.

sections.title: How Schedules Will Be Published
sections.content:
Heafner and Alex McKenzie of BBN agree the schedules should be published as an RFC updating NIC Memo 5767 (ARPA Network Site Status). Heafner collects the information by phone, mail or NIC and sends it to McKenzie for technical editing and publication. The forthcoming Resource Notebook (NIC 5760) covers service use and job numbers, so the schedules may reference it but will not duplicate it.

Rand's role, as RFC 111 states, is to help test implementations remotely. That testing will be short term and will not go beyond what is in RFC 111. Readers are invited to contact Heafner or Eric Harslem.
sections.eli5: One person gathers everyone's dates, a second person tidies them, and then they are posted for all to see.
